post_lock_changes.reason: Baseline replaced after the holdout run showed the first-draft baseline ('naive', kept as arm 0) assigned narration words to numeric columns: a design flaw, not a fair 'straightforward' parser. Baseline v1 was written without running it on the holdout first.
post_lock_changes.affects: baseline and validated arms; full arm unaffected

post_lock_changes.reason: Two bugs in the robust extractor found by diagnosing locked-holdout failures: (1) indicator-column window 4pt too tight when header is centred and values left-aligned (layout F); (2) header-free fallback counted only dated lines as rows (layout G with blank dates). Added behind fixes=True; fixes=False is the locked behaviour.
post_lock_changes.affects: arm 3b only; arm 3 (locked) runs with fixes=False

post_lock_changes.reason: Baseline v1.1: v1 treated any lone 'D'/'C' word anywhere in the row as the Dr/Cr marker (a narration such as 'JOSEPH D SOUZA' flipped a credit to a debit). Found by debugging on DEV fixtures; now the marker is only read inside the indicator column. Baseline v1 had been run once on holdout (concurrently with this fix); the holdout baseline arms were re-run with v1.1.

End-to-end review after the holdout: (1) fixes=True only: a transaction whose narration reads like 'closing balance ...' is no longer swallowed as a summary row; the summary finder skips dated lines; short statements (a column with 1-2 entries) keep their amount columns. (2) all modes: process() is fail-safe, any exception while reading/processing returns UNSUPPORTED (a fuzz run found an uncaught PyMuPDF 'malformed page tree' crash). (3) balance_break flags carry the amount the printed balances imply. (4) CSV export neutralises formula injection; zero amounts exported correctly. (5) dead variables removed.
post_lock_changes.affects: Arm 3 (locked, fixes=False) and arms 0-2 re-run after these changes: 0 per-case differences across 780 case/arm results on dev+holdout. Arm 3b re-run: also 0 differences (the new edge cases are not present in the benchmark fixtures; covered by unit tests instead).
